chunks: And it was narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from his father, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I have young children with me, and I fear the cold for them. From where should they enter ihram?”
So he said: “Take them to al-ʿArj, and let them enter ihram from there, for when you come to al-ʿArj, you will have entered Tihāmah.”
Then he said: “If you fear for them, then take them to al-Juḥfah.”

key_terms.الْبَرْدَ: the cold weather feared for the children
key_terms.الْجُحْفَةَ: another location mentioned as an alternative place for ihram
key_terms.الْعَرْجَ: a location mentioned as a place from which ihram may be assumed
key_terms.تِهَامَةَ: the lowland region entered upon reaching al-ʿArj
key_terms.يُحْرِمُونَ: they enter the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: From where may young children enter ihram for hajj if there is fear of cold?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding the miqat of children during hajj when cold weather may harm them. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permits delaying their ihram to al-ʿArj, and if fear remains, to al-Juḥfah, showing consideration for hardship in acts of worship.
